chitchat: Keel planes a curl off the edge of a plank, sights along it, and planes another.
He drives a fastening home in three blows, never four.
Water slops up the slot and knocks a fender against the stocks.
He stops, listens to an outboard going past outside, and shakes his head.
He writes a figure on the slate by the bench, rubs it out with his thumb and writes a smaller one.
description: A big man in his sixties in a scorched leather apron, with sawdust in the hair on his forearms. There is a carpenter's pencil behind one ear and another behind the other that he has forgotten about. He talks to the hull on the stocks more than he talks to customers.

buy.text: "Vaskin hulls, off the same list the glass place sells from." He drops a catalogue on the bench, open. "Same price, too. I don't build them, I just sell them. She comes with a full tank and the first free berth in this yard."

bye.text: "Mind the stage on your way out. It moves."

drive.text: "Go where she's lying and board. That puts you aboard. helm puts you at the wheel, and the controls card comes up the first time." "K is the key, and she won't start with the lever open. From the log, conn start, then conn with a bearing or a bell." "Coming home, stop alongside a berth and disembark. That ties her up. Do it on open water and you're swimming. If she dies out there, tow brings her home, and you settle the bill before she goes out again."

fuel.text: "End of the outer stage. Hand pump on a drum." He mimes cranking it. "Come alongside, stop, and fuel. You pay by the unit, so a bigger tank costs more to fill."

hire.text: "Two hours, a full tank, one at a time." He nods at the keys on nails behind the bench. "Tie her up anywhere in this yard when you're done and she's back, or bring me the key sooner. No paint and no names on a hire."

hull.text:
"Forty feet. Larch on oak." He runs a hand along the planking where it stops. "I started her in the shed on Lever Lane. It took four of us and a flatbed to get her down here."

He looks out through the open doors at the water.

"She goes in when she's done. She's nearer it now than she's ever been."

keep.text: "Three ways, and the roof's the dear one." He points with the mallet. "In here, in the slot under the roof, room for two: that's where I can work on her properly. Outside on the hard, on a cradle: cheapest. Or afloat on the stages, alongside, five berths." "Stand at a berth and berth reads you the board. berth and her name moves her in. boats tells you where she is now. Whatever the glass place charges, I charge six-tenths."

return.text: He holds out a hand for the key.

root.text: "Buying, hiring, berthing or broke?" Keel doesn't put the mallet down.

text_by_relation.familiar: "Kettle's on the stove in the back." He doesn't look up from the plank. "What's she done?"
text_by_relation.first:
A big man in a leather apron is fitting a plank to the hull on the stocks. He finishes the stroke before he looks round.

"Keel." He points the mallet at things as he names them. "Boats for sale and boats for hire, across that bench. Berths on the stages and the hard outside. Anything wrong with a hull, I fix it in here."

"Same boats as the glass place on the west shore, and the same work. Six-tenths of the price, and the roof leaks."
text_by_relation.known: "You." He sets the mallet down on the plank. "What is it this time?"

work.text: "I'm in here from six in the morning to midnight." He taps the bench. "Stand in here with me and refit, and I'll put the hull back to sound wherever she's lying in this yard. Servicing, paint and a name, she has to be under this roof: berth her in the slot, or bring her in and stop. Then refit service, refit paint or refit name." "Away from here you patch her yourself. I sell the patches."
